sentences.en: Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 你好,这是6分钟英语 从英国广播公司学习英语。

sentences.en: I'm Neil. And I'm Becca. Now, today, we’re going to be talking about the very serious topic of war and how it affects children.
sentences.zh: 我是尼尔,我是贝卡,今天,我们要讨论战争这个非常严重的话题,以及战争对儿童的影响。

sentences.en: Some of the discussions you hear will mention death and trauma.
sentences.zh: 你听到的一些讨论会提到死亡和创伤。

sentences.en: We won’t go into detail, but if you think you feel may uncomfortable, you can check the transcript for this episode before listening to it on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 我们不会细说, 但如果你觉得自己可能不舒服, 你可以先查看这集的笔录,

sentences.en: Yes. And remember, you'll find all this episode's vocabulary, along with a free worksheet, and many other 6 Minute English episodes on our website.
sentences.zh: 是的,记住,你会在我们的网站上 找到这集的词汇,还有一份免费的工作表, 还有许多其他的6分钟英语片段。

sentences.en: Again, that’s bbclearningenglish.com. The most recent figure from 2024 says that 520 million children are living in conflict zones.
sentences.zh: 这也是bbclearningenglish.com。 2024年的最新数字显示,有5.2亿儿童生活在冲突地区。

sentences.en: That's about one in every five children worldwide.
sentences.zh: 全世界每五个孩子中就有一个

sentences.en: In this episode, we'll hear from Fergal Keane on the BBC World Service Programme The Global Story.
sentences.zh: 在这集中,我们将从Fergal Keane听到英国广播公司世界服务节目《全球故事》。

sentences.en: Fergal is a BBC reporter known best for reporting from war zones around the world and, as a result, developed PTSD, a type of stress disorder.
sentences.zh: Fergal是英国广播公司最著名的记者,报道来自世界各地的战区,因此,他患上了创伤后应激障碍症。

sentences.en: We'll be finding out what PTSD stands for at the end of the programme.
sentences.zh: 我们会在节目结束时 找出创伤后应激障碍代表什么

sentences.en: Now, in the clips we’ll hear journalist Asma Khalid asks Fergal Keane about his own experience with childhood trauma.
sentences.zh: 现在,我们会听到记者Asma Khalid问Fergal Keane自己如何经历童年创伤。

sentences.en: Fergal grew up in a home with an alcoholic father.
sentences.zh: Fergal在一个有酒鬼父亲的家里长大

sentences.en: Asma wanted to know how his own trauma affected his reporting on the experiences of children in warzones: I was hyper-vigilant from the very earliest age, obviously watching out, you know, am I under threat, is there a danger to me here?
sentences.zh: 阿斯玛想知道他自己所受的创伤如何影响他关于战区儿童经历的报道:我从小就非常谨慎,显然,我受到威胁,我在这里是否有危险?

sentences.en: Fergal mentions that he was hyper-vigilant because was in dangerous situations as a child.
sentences.zh: Fergal提到,他非常谨慎,因为从小就处于危险境地。

sentences.en: The adjective vigilant means to always be careful to notice things, particularly when there is a possibility of danger.
sentences.zh: 提高警惕的形容词意味着始终要小心注意事情,特别是在有危险的可能性时。

sentences.en: Yes. And the prefix hyper- expresses that there is a lot of or even too much of something.
sentences.zh: 是的,前缀高端表示 有很多甚或太多的东西。

sentences.en: Though neutral, it is often used in negative or critical contexts.
sentences.zh: 虽然是中性的,但往往在消极或危急情况下使用。

sentences.en: So, hyper-vigilant means very, very careful and thoughtful.
sentences.zh: 所以,超敏锐意味着非常,非常小心和周到。

sentences.en: Hypervigilance, the noun, is a state of extreme alertness and sensitivity to surroundings, possibly of extreme anxiety.
sentences.zh: 超常警惕,名人, 是一种极端的警惕状态 和对周围的敏感, 可能是极端的焦虑。

sentences.en: Now let’s hear from Fergal as he talks about research on the experience of children in warzones: I mean, they disagree about a few things, but on this they' re absolutely of one mind.
sentences.zh: 现在让我们听听Fergal在谈论关于儿童在战区经历的研究:我的意思是,他们在一些问题上意见不一,但对于这一点,他们绝对是一个想法。

sentences.en: And that is that you can't recover from war trauma if you're living with continuing trauma.
sentences.zh: 这就是说,如果你生活在持续的创伤中, 你无法从战争创伤中恢复过来。

sentences.en: Fergal mentions that ‘they’, the researchers, disagree about their findings.
sentences.zh: 研究者Fergal提到,

sentences.en: But they' re absolutely of one mind when considering the recovery of war trauma.
sentences.zh: 但考虑到战争创伤的恢复,他们绝对是一心一意的

sentences.en: If you are of one mind, you are of a group of people that share the same opinion, desire, or viewpoint on a matter.
sentences.zh: 如果你只有一个想法, 你是一个群体 具有相同的见解, 渴望,或观点 在一个事项上。

sentences.en: Researchers may disagree on whether the experiences of children in warzones is improving, but on the point of recovery, they are of one mind on that you can’t recover from war trauma if you continue living with it.
sentences.zh: 研究者们可能对于儿童在战区的经历是否在改善意见不一,但从康复的角度来看,他们的一个想法是,如果你继续生活在战争创伤中,他们就无法从中恢复。

sentences.en: Fergal goes on to talk about some of the ways in which these children might be helped: And so there's a new field of theory, well I mean relatively new field of theory which encourages children to slowly and carefully try to confront obviously not death and massacre again, but things like learning to sleep alone, not having to sleep with a parent because that's what they did during the war because they were so consistently terrified.
sentences.zh: Fergal接着谈到一些可以帮助这些儿童的方式: 因此,有一个新的理论领域, 我指的是相对新的理论领域,它鼓励儿童 缓慢和小心地努力面对死亡和屠杀, 显然不是再次, 而是学习独自睡觉, 不必和父母上床, 因为他们在战争期间 一直很害怕。

sentences.en: Now, it sounds like a simple thing, but as anybody who's tried to put a child to sleep, who's had a nightmare, a child who hasn't been traumatised will know it's very difficult.
sentences.zh: 听上去很简单 但当有人试图让孩子睡觉 做恶梦时 一个没有受创伤的孩子会知道这很困难

sentences.en: Fergal says that children should be encouraged to slowly and carefully try to confront their experiences.
sentences.zh: Fergal说,应当鼓励儿童缓慢和认真地努力面对他们的经历。

sentences.en: To confront something is to meet with it or deal with it.
sentences.zh: 面对的东西是 与它见面或处理它。

sentences.en: For the children to confront their terrifying experiences, they must start with more simple things, like learning to sleep alone.
sentences.zh: 为了让儿童面对他们可怕的经历,他们必须从更简单的事物开始,例如学会单独睡觉。

sentences.en: Sleeping alone seems simple enough, but Fergal compares the experiences of a children of in a warzone to that of children who have nightmares.
sentences.zh: 单独睡觉似乎很简单,但Fergal将一个在战区的儿童的经历比作做恶梦的儿童的经历。

sentences.en: Yes, and a nightmare is a very scary or upsetting dream.
sentences.zh: 是的 做恶梦是很可怕的 也是令人沮丧的梦

sentences.en: It can also be used metaphorically to describe unpleasant events or experiences.
sentences.zh: 也可以用比喻来描述不愉快的事件或经历。

sentences.en: Now, let’s hear Fergal talk about what he has learned from reporting on children in warzones: The big lesson is that, given a chance, the human spirit, and especially children, are phenomenally resilient.
sentences.zh: 现在让我们来听听Fergal关于他从报告战区儿童情况中学到的东西:一个重大教训是,只要有机会,人类精神,特别是儿童,就具有惊人的弹性。

sentences.en: Fergal describes the children as being phenomenally resilient.
sentences.zh: Fergal认为儿童具有惊人的适应力。

sentences.en: The noun phenomenon, or phenomena in its plural form, refers to an observable fact or event that can be experienced through the senses.
sentences.zh: 名词现象或其多元形式的现象是指可以通过感官感受到的可观察到的事实或事件。

sentences.en: The adverb phenomenally describes something being done or felt in an extreme or surprising way.
sentences.zh: 副词以极端或令人吃惊的方式描述了正在做或感觉到的事情。

sentences.en: To be resilient is to be able to recover from and come back from something difficult or bad that's happened.
sentences.zh: 适应力是能够从已经发生的 困难或糟糕的事情中恢复过来

sentences.en: So, Fergal says that children can be surprisingly positive despite the negative things happening around them.
sentences.zh: Fergal说,尽管他们周围发生了负面的事情,但孩子们还是会出奇地呈阳性。

sentences.en: They are phenomenally resilient. A result of these negative things could be PTSD.
sentences.zh: 它们具有惊人的弹性。这些负面因素的结果可能是创伤后应激障碍。

sentences.en: Earlier we mentioned PTSD and it stands for post-traumatic stress disorder.
sentences.zh: 我们早些时候提到创伤后应激障碍。

sentences.en: Yes, and the P in PTSD stands for post-, as we've just heard.
sentences.zh: 是的 创伤后应激障碍中P代表了后期, 正如我们刚刚听到的。

sentences.en: And the prefix post- expresses something that happens after or as a result of the event it's attached to.
sentences.zh: 而前缀后... 表达的东西 发生后 或因事件的结果 它的附属。

sentences.en: Now, let’s recap the vocabulary. We first had hyper-vigilant, that is to be very careful or maybe almost too careful to notice things, particularly when there is a possibility of danger.
sentences.zh: 现在,让我们来回顾一下词汇。 我们首先非常谨慎,那就是非常小心,或者几乎太小心,无法注意到一些事情,特别是在有危险的可能性的时候。

sentences.en: To be of one mind is to be part of a group of people that share the same opinion, desire, or viewpoint on a matter.
sentences.zh: 一种思想就是成为在某一问题上有相同观点、愿望或观点的群体的一部分。

sentences.en: We had confront something. That is to meet with it or deal with it.
sentences.zh: 我们面对了某些事情,那就是要面对它或者处理它。

sentences.en: A nightmare is a scary or upsetting dream.
sentences.zh: 恶梦是可怕的,或令人沮丧的。

sentences.en: To do something phenomenally is to do it in an extreme or surprising way.
sentences.zh: 做一件奇怪的事情就是 以一种极端或令人惊讶的方式去做

sentences.en: And to be resilient is to be able to recover and come back from something difficult or bad.
sentences.zh: 具有弹性的是能够从困难或坏事中恢复回来。

sentences.en: That's happened once again. Our six minutes are up.
sentences.zh: 这又发生了 我们的六分钟到了

sentences.en: You'll find a quiz and a worksheet to practice the vocabulary we've learnt from this episode on our website BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 你会找到一个测验和工作单 来练习我们从BBC网站上学到的词汇

sentences.en: Goodbye for now. Bye.
sentences.zh: 再见,再见
